Sysctl checks and sets kernel parameters for general, XDP, and socket network modes.

# Purpose
This file defines the `sysctl` configuration stage for the configure system. It checks and, when needed, sets Linux kernel parameters under `/proc/sys` before the application runs. The stage first requests the `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` capability in [`init_perm`](<#init_perm>), because writing to kernel parameters requires that privilege. It then uses `fd_file_util_read_ulong` and `fd_file_util_write_ulong` to read and update selected sysctl values, and it reports errors with the configure logging and result macros.

The file manages three parameter groups: general kernel settings in `params`, XDP network settings in `xdp_params`, and socket network buffer settings in `sock_params`. The [`init`](<#init>) function enforces minimum values for required parameters, while [`check`](<#check>) verifies that the current system meets the expected values and returns a configuration failure if not. The behavior depends on `config->net.provider`: for `xdp`, it checks XDP-related sysctls; for `socket`, it checks buffer sizes from the socket configuration; for other values, it reports an unknown provider error. The exported `fd_cfg_stage_sysctl` structure registers this logic as a configure stage.
